stem: If a polynomial $P(x)$ is divided by $x-{=p}$, the remainder is ${=r1}$, and when divided by $x+{=q}$, the remainder is ${=r2}$. Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $(x-{=p})(x+{=q})$.
solution: Write $P(x) = (x-{=p})(x+{=q})Q(x) + ax + b$, since the divisor has degree 2 and the remainder has the form $ax+b$.
Subtract the second equation from the first: ${=s}a = {=r1 - r2}$, so $a = {=a}$.
notes: Basic entry: factored divisor with roots p and -q; remainder values are built from a chosen ax+b so a, b are always integers. a is nonzero so the remainder is genuinely linear; b may be 0.
